decision_rule.admitted: ADMITTED if and only if all four hold against the SEALED ANCHOR's score artifact: (1) the CI95 LOWER bound of the paired official pooled SLU-F1 delta is greater than 0; (2) intent is non-inferior at the own-null margin -- its CI95 lower bound exceeds -1.0051; (3) the TRAIN symmetric scorer slurp-slu-f1-normalized-v1-train agrees in sign with the unprojected primary; and (4) no scenario loses intent beyond the null band -- no scenario's paired intent CI95 upper bound lies below zero.
decision_rule.harmful_first: HARMFUL is read FIRST (owner decision 25, Method B): only by a MEASURED loss -- a point estimate of the official pooled SLU-F1 delta or of the intent delta below -h (-1.1218 / -1.0051), or a CI95 UPPER bound below zero. An interval that straddles zero with the point estimate inside the margin is NOT harmful; it reads NEUTRAL with 'non-inferiority not proven' stated in those words.
decision_rule.neutral: NEUTRAL otherwise. Under owner decision 30 a NEUTRAL or HARMFUL one-factor read advances the headroom-exhausted streak; a beneficial but not CI95-proven movement is RECORDED as such (owner decision 25) and never claimed as an admission.

The retired imported DEV-1000 half-widths are never used.

not_claimed: No superiority, generalization, paper-scale or held-out claim. TRAIN Fold A is an exposed discovery roster and every claim of this cell stops at it. Fold B, DEV-1000 and the test split stay untouched and unread.

No gold of an evaluated row enters the block, at build time or at runtime. The only text of an evaluated row that can appear is the draft's own entity TYPE names, which the consumer already holds in the sealed draft immediately above.

No claim that the Reviewer ACTS on the block. The cell measures whether the loop's outcome moves; whether the Reviewer's criticism changes because of the audit, or for some other reason, is not separable here.
No attribution to one flag. The four move together; the per-flag table is a diagnostic, not four separate admissions.
No claim about the A3 audit's own counts. They bound what the block can touch; they are never a predicted gain.
No claim that a larger or differently thresholded table would do better. The thresholds are the registered defaults and are not tuned here; changing one is a new cell.

No claim that the retained finite-completion rows are comparable to the anchor's. The anchor flew without the key; its receipt records zero such rows, and any non-zero count on this side is reported, never reconciled.
No claim that the block's token cost is free. It is reported per role beside the anchor's.
A structural smoke result is never a quality result, and this is not a bar attempt. The verdict states the official pooled SLU the arm reaches and whether it clears 64.00 as a FACT, never as a claim.

Nothing about task quality from the predecessor. Its 2,016 contacts were never scored and never read; no partial read is permitted; the 378 rows it completed reach a number only through the one official score of the complete merged 1,080-row manifest.

No sub-population claim about kept versus flown rows, and no claim that a resumed pass is a cleaner pass than a re-flown one. 378 rows keep the batch composition they were drawn under and 702 rows are drawn under a new one; greedy decoding is not bitwise reproducible across batch compositions, and this package makes no claim that the effect of that is zero.

No claim that retaining a row whose Reviewer found nothing is evidence that the row is as good as one whose Reviewer reviewed. The ReAct-exhaustion disposition is a failure-mode repair, not a mechanism, and its counts are diagnostics.

resume.root_cause: A harness defect, named to a component. With the Reviewer slot-audit attachment armed, 2 of 410 Reviewer visits spent all three of their ReAct iterations calling saea-tool-task-contract-v1 with {} and never produced an answer; the pinned framework returned its own 'Max iterations reached without completion' literal under result_type 'error', and reproduction.ojw.native_episode._ApplyRole raised NativeEpisodeError ('review node did not return an answer') at node reviewer_1_state, because the graph had no word for 'the reviewer found nothing'. Not the roster, the prompt, the knowledge, the retrieval, the budget, the geometry, the scoring or the question: the request bytes already transmitted were the registered ones, the flight worktree was clean at c905ddf0, the prepared artifact verified identity_ok, and three EARLIER length-capped Reviewer completions in the very same flight were retained by the armed finite_completion_policy (item E13), which is the same class of repair one item earlier.

the_one_declared_repair.asymmetry: The sealed anchor flew without the key; the comparator reached ReAct iteration 3/3 on ZERO visits (B1r comparator log: 1,092 visits at 1/3, 0 at 3/3), so on the comparator side the key would have changed nothing. Measured, not assumed.
the_one_declared_repair.renders_no_request_byte: rails.runner reads it once into core NativeEpisodeSpec. It fires ONLY on a visit that would otherwise abort the flight: the exhausted visit ends with an empty finding (state['review'] == ''), custody of its contacts is kept in role_visits, the Planner routes normally, nothing is retried and no prompt byte of any other contact moves. A committed test asserts the framework's literal never reaches a rendered request, and another composes byte-identical requests on both arms for a row whose roles all answer.
the_one_declared_repair.scope: REACT_EXHAUSTION_STAGES == {'review'} and nothing else; Solver, Planner and Perception keep their pre-E22 raise.

resume.what_does_not_change: The same 1,080-row TRAIN Fold A roster, the same SLURP-EVO-FOLD-A-V2, the same split identity, the same ordered ids; both knowledge stores, the arm, the policy, the whole native episode including the one factor native_episode.reviewer_audit and its three thresholds, every instruction template, phase_tools, the scorers, the model fragment, the serving geometry, the promoted packets, the resident session and both WAVE R7 speech-feature identity strings are byte-identical to the aborted arm's. The two identity strings are HELD, not minted fresh: they ride the audited payload as ORG/CONTROL provenance and the 378 kept rows already carry the aborted attempt's values.

the_analysis_and_its_boundary.attachment: sealed-draft (item E19). The block is appended after the sealed Solver response, separated by one newline. Every flag is computed by the HARNESS from the parsed draft and the pinned table; every substituted value is a construction count, a construction share, a released convention sentence, a closed flag name, or an entity TYPE the draft or the table already carries.
the_analysis_and_its_boundary.construction_pool: the governed SLURP TRAIN split MINUS every utterance with a recording in TRAIN Fold A, TRAIN Fold B or DEV-1000, and the 2026-09-13 exclusion: 9,354 utterances. The released table carries counts and shares only -- no filler, no sentence, no utterance id, no recording and no gold of any evaluated row -- which is why it is committed rather than kept under SPEECHRL_DATA_DIR.

flags.EMPTY-DRAFT: an entity-free draft for an intent whose construction rows carry an entity at least as often as empty_draft_min_entity_row_share
flags.MISSING-COMMON: an entity type attested with the drafted intent on at least missing_common_min_row_share of its construction rows and absent from the draft
flags.REPRESENTATION: a filler that violates saea-spoken-form-v1 (no ASCII digit, no colon, no slash) for a type whose released convention is spoken
flags.TYPE-UNSEEN: an entity TYPE in the draft that the construction table never attests with the drafted intent

the_analysis_and_its_boundary.zero_contacts: the block makes no model, tokenizer, encoder, scorer, tool, server or network contact, so the bounded contact ceiling stays 11 and every budget is the anchor's, unchanged
